items.title: No more black screen from a Windows PC
items.detail: Some PCs, often laptops with two graphics chips, sent no picture at all: only the pointer moved. Annex now checks that the PC's video encoder really produces frames and switches to another one if it doesn't.

items.title: The log says why a picture doesn't arrive
items.detail: If no video goes out in the first seconds, annex.log names the likely cause, and the PC's log names the video encoder it chose.

items.title: Saidev Dhal is credited on Windows too
items.detail: The installer and Apps & features name both makers, Nalinish Ranjan and Saidev Dhal.

items.title: A Mac's screen shows on PCs without working HEVC
items.detail: Annex checks that the PC's HEVC decoder really starts before asking for HEVC; otherwise the picture comes as H.264.

items.title: The notch drop forgets a computer that's gone
items.detail: After sharing is turned off, dragging a file no longer offers to send it to the computer that was connected.

items.title: What's new on Windows looks like the Mac's
items.detail: Each version's changes in tidy groups, scrolling inside a window that fits the screen.

items.title: Windows looks more like the Mac
items.detail: The rings behind "Waiting for a computer…" pulse, and computer names on the live card sit in clean capsules.

items.title: A Mac's screen shows on PCs without working HEVC
items.detail: Annex checks that the PC's HEVC decoder really starts before asking for HEVC; otherwise the picture comes as H.264.

items.title: The notch drop forgets a computer that's gone
items.detail: After sharing is turned off, dragging a file no longer offers to send it to the computer that was connected.

items.title: What's new scrolls on Windows
items.detail: It fits the window instead of growing past the screen.

items.title: Clean name capsules on the Windows live card
items.detail: The computers' names sit in proper capsules, like on the Mac.

items.title: A Mac trackpad scrolls the right way on another Mac
items.detail: Controlling a Mac from a Mac, the trackpad and Magic Mouse scroll as on your own Mac.

items.title: Reverse Mouse Wheel is back
items.detail: On Windows and Linux, a plain mouse wheel turns the way it does on a PC. The trackpad and Magic Mouse keep natural scrolling. It's in Settings → Advanced → Viewing.

items.title: Mac shortcuts go to the Mac you control
items.detail: With the viewer in front, ⌘Space, ⌘Tab, ⌃←/→, Mission Control and screenshot keys work on the other Mac. Click away, or swipe to another desktop, and they're yours again. ⌃⌥⇧Q disconnects.

items.title: Windows and Linux shortcuts go to the computer you control
items.detail: With the viewer in front, the Windows key, Alt+Tab and Print Screen (Super and Alt+Tab on Linux) work on the other computer. Click away and they're yours again. Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Q disconnects.

items.title: Scrolling turns the way it does on your Mac
items.detail: Reverse Mouse Wheel is gone: on every computer you control, scrolling now follows your Mac's own natural-scrolling setting, trackpad and mouse wheel alike.

items.title: The picture no longer freezes while the pointer moves
items.detail: When a moment of a session was lost on the way, the picture could stay stuck for up to 30 seconds while the pointer kept moving. The viewer now asks again until the picture is back, usually within a second.

items.title: A steadier picture on a fast connection
items.detail: After lowering the quality because frames were lost, Annex no longer climbs straight back to where they were lost. It waits a moment and climbs slowly near that point.

items.title: More direct connections with a code
items.detail: While a code waits, Annex keeps the way in open, so a code typed minutes later can still connect directly instead of through the relay.

items.title: Relay sessions left today
items.detail: The sharing page shows how many of today's 10 relay sessions are left, and says when they're used up. Your own relay and server have no limit.

items.title: A sharper picture over the internet
items.detail: Annex no longer lowers the quality for the odd lost frame, and climbs back faster.

items.title: HEVC when both computers support it
items.detail: The picture goes as HEVC, sharper at the same speed, between any two computers that support it. Otherwise H.264. It's in Settings.

items.title: The relay at full quality
items.detail: Used only when a direct connection is blocked, now with the same picture as direct and no 20-minute limit. 10 sessions a day per computer, end to end encrypted.

items.title: More direct internet connections
items.detail: When the sharing computer's internet provider gives each connection its own port, Annex now finds it, so fewer sessions need the relay.

items.title: Clearer logs for internet connections
items.detail: If a connection over the internet is slow or uses the relay, the log now helps find out why. Sessions stay end to end encrypted either way.

items.title: Sharing stays on or off
items.detail: On Linux, a share that failed right after starting could flip on and off by itself. It no longer does.

items.title: GNOME: no freeze at login
items.detail: Annex starts 15 seconds after login, so the desktop can't freeze on graphics drivers that did.

items.title: GNOME: headless sharing keeps working
items.detail: With No one at this screen on, the screen no longer locks while Annex shares it, and a closed screen share reopens for the next viewer.

items.title: Natural trackpad scrolling
items.detail: Reverse Mouse Wheel now reverses only a mouse wheel. Trackpad and Magic Mouse scrolling stays natural.

items.title: Linux switches and icon
items.detail: Switches look right on every theme, and Annex's icon shows in menus, the taskbar and the window switcher.

items.title: No more echo
items.detail: With Send my microphone on, neither side hears itself come back any more. Headphones are no longer needed.

items.title: A cleaner microphone
items.detail: Steady background noise, like a fan, is filtered out of your voice. Music and videos from the other computer are left alone.

items.title: Sound and microphone, device by device
items.detail: Each paired device has Can hear this computer's sound and Its microphone plays here, under the mouse and keyboard switch. Both start on.

items.title: A full command line on Linux
items.detail: Control Annex from a terminal or over SSH: annex status, annex set <setting> on|off, annex devices, annex pin and more. Run annex help.

items.title: Tailscale computers show in Nearby on the Mac
items.detail: Annex could not read Tailscale's list of computers when opened as an app, so Nearby showed only the same Wi-Fi.

items.title: The log explains a missing computer
items.detail: It says how many computers Tailscale listed, how many answered, and why Tailscale couldn't be asked.

items.title: Hear the other computer
items.detail: While you view a computer, you hear what it plays. Turn it off in Settings → Advanced → Sound.

items.title: Talk through the other computer
items.detail: Turn on Send my microphone in Settings → Advanced → Sound and your voice plays on the computer you're viewing. Use headphones to avoid an echo.

items.title: Annex Microphone on Linux
items.detail: On a Linux computer you control, your microphone shows up as Annex Microphone, so Zoom, Meet or Discord there can use it for calls.

items.title: Pause or unsend a file
items.detail: Files you're sending show Pause and Unsend in the island at the top of the screen. Unsending deletes what had arrived.

items.title: Annex for Linux looks and works like the Mac
items.detail: A dark window with grouped settings, the quality picker, update checks, live session stats and more.

items.title: Smooth video on slow connections
items.detail: On a slow link Annex now stays live instead of falling seconds behind, sending a smaller picture until the link speeds up again.

items.title: The Mac's notch glows as soon as you drag a file
items.detail: Before, it only lit up once the file reached it.

items.title: Copy here, paste there
items.detail: While you control another computer, what you copy on one can be pasted on the other: text and pictures. Passwords from password managers stay on the computer they were copied on. Turn it off in Settings → Clipboard and files.

items.title: Send files by dragging them
items.detail: Drag files or folders onto the window showing the other computer. They arrive in its Downloads folder, exactly as sent.

items.title: Drop files at the top of the screen
items.detail: Start dragging a file and a silver island pops out at the top of the screen (from the notch on a Mac). Bring the file close and drop it there to send it. Files coming in show there too.

items.title: Scrolling feels the same everywhere
items.detail: A Mac controlling Windows or Linux now scrolls the same way it does on the Mac. Change it in Settings → Viewing.

items.title: A log that explains what went wrong
items.detail: Settings → Developer → Show log files. When something fails, the moments before it are saved in the crashes folder. Turn on Verbose logging while chasing a problem. Only your account can read the log, and it never holds what you type, copy or send.

items.title: Smoother scrolling on a Mac you control
items.detail: Small scrolls no longer judder.

items.title: Linux Extend matches the viewer's screen
items.detail: The extra display uses the viewer's scale, so text is the right size. Change it in Settings.

items.title: Annex on a Mac no longer opens Tailscale
items.detail: Looking for nearby computers no longer starts the Tailscale app.
